basics.name: Mark Tripoli
basics.summary: Staff Software Engineer who architects and builds distributed systems, decentralized platforms, and high-throughput infrastructure. Currently building Atlas—a decentralized platform (SDK + infrastructure) for building mission applications, with mesh networking, multi-transport, DIDs, and an autonomous agent runtime for cloud and edge—and AOK (Adyton Operations Kit) at Adyton. Pragmatic about AI/LLM adoption—uses it aggressively to accelerate POCs, automate toil, and return engineering time to hard problems, while maintaining that production systems need architectural determinism, human oversight, and real software discipline. Track record of designing systems that scale—from notification pipelines processing 1M+ messages in minutes to build orchestration platforms serving thousands of developers daily. Equally comfortable writing Rust, Go, or Python as leading technical vision across teams. Career spans defense tech, big tech, startups, and a decade of railroad and military operations.

work.name: Adyton
work.summary: Staff Software Engineer building Atlas and AOK (Adyton Operations Kit). Atlas is a decentralized platform—SDK and infrastructure—for building mission applications. It provides mesh networking, multi-transport (BLE, WiFi, LoRa, satellite), decentralized identity (DIDs), offline-first architecture, and an autonomous agent runtime for cloud and edge, giving identities and authorization to sensors, effectors, phones, and agents. The Atlas Mission App is a Flutter implementation with Rust gateways and other deployables built on the platform. Building self-sovereign infrastructure including a Signal SVR2-inspired identity backup service using AWS Nitro Enclaves, OPRF, and Noise NK for zero-knowledge PIN-gated recovery of BIP39 cryptographic identities. AOK is Adyton's operational suite, featuring a NATS JetStream-based async notification platform processing 1M+ notifications in under 10 minutes via Twilio, WhatsApp, and Email, with muster-message ask-and-respond patterns and webhook delivery tracking.
highlights: Architecting Atlas: a decentralized platform (SDK + infrastructure) for building mission applications, with mesh networking and multi-transport (BLE, WiFi, LoRa, satellite).
Implementing decentralized identity (DIDs) with authorization for sensors, effectors, mobile devices, and agents across Atlas.
Building an autonomous agent runtime for cloud and edge—identity-bound agents with decentralized authorization, deployable on-demand.

Designed and built self-sovereign identity backup service (Go) inspired by Signal's SVR2—OPRF-based zero-knowledge PIN recovery of BIP39 entropy via AWS Nitro Enclaves, Noise NK tunnels, and Ristretto255.
Building AOK (Adyton Operations Kit) with NATS JetStream-based async notification platform handling 1M+ bursty notifications in <10 minutes across Twilio, WhatsApp, and Email.
Designing muster message product feature within AOK for ask-and-respond patterns with webhook delivery status ingestion.
Leveraging AI/LLM tooling to accelerate delivery and automate engineering toil while enforcing architectural determinism and human oversight for production systems.

projects.name: Atlas Principal Storage — Self-Sovereign Identity Backup
projects.description: Signal SVR2-inspired identity backup service built in Go for Atlas. Allows users to securely back up BIP39 cryptographic identity entropy to AWS Nitro Enclaves with PIN-gated zero-knowledge recovery. Uses OPRF (Ristretto255, RFC 9497) so the enclave never learns the PIN, Noise NK end-to-end tunnels with remote attestation, and NitroTPM seal/unseal for enclave state persistence.
highlights: AWS Nitro Enclaves
OPRF (Ristretto255)
Noise NK + attestation
BIP39 entropy backup
Zero-knowledge PIN recovery
Go
